title: Rep. Moore: Congress Faces Packed Post-Midterm Agenda
title_cn: Rep. Moore: Congress Faces Packed Post-Midterm Agenda
summary: Rep. Blake Moore (R-UT) says candidates need to be candid with voters about higher energy prices and the challenges driving them. Rep. Moore says Congress should take up bipartisan permitting reform after the midterms as lawmakers look for ways to address energy costs. Rep. Moore says reconciliation also needs to be addressed despite a packed lame-duck agenda that includes defense authorization and appropriations. Rep. Moore says any reconciliation package would likely change from earlier drafts and could include legislation he says would save hundreds of billions of dollars by targeting fraud. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Thomas: Alaska Controversy Could Shift Senate Race
title_cn: Thomas: Alaska Controversy Could Shift Senate Race
summary: John Thomas, Nestpoint managing director and veteran Republican pollster and Strategist, says the controversy surrounding another Dan Sullivan on Alaska's Senate ballot could materially affect a race within the margin of error by undermining voter trust. Thomas says Republicans can be difficult for pollsters to reach and that some close races could break differently than current polling suggests. Thomas says Vivek Ramaswamy's controversial Ohio ad was in poor taste and hurt Republicans on the ticket, while predicting Ken Paxton will narrowly win in Texas. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stevenson Says Fed Is Waiting to See Economy Slow
title_cn: Stevenson Says Fed Is Waiting to See Economy Slow
summary: Betsey Stevenson, Professor of Public Policy and Economics at the University of Michigan's Ford School and former Chief Economist of the Department of Labor, says the Fed's decision to leave rates unchanged is puzzling because another increase is still likely. Stevenson says policymakers may be waiting to see whether the economy slows further before raising rates again. Stevenson says uncertainty around the midterm elections and potential changes in fiscal policy could also affect how high rates ultimately need to go. She speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
